result.title: Physics-informed neural networks for spacecraft trajectory optimization with exact boundary conditions
result.summary: We use neural networks to optimize trajectories by modeling the position as a function of time and minimizing the thrust with respect to the network parameters. This corresponds to an unsupervised training procedure in which physical laws are incorporated directly into the optimization objective. In standard physics-informed neural networks, initial and terminal states are enforced through additional weighted loss terms, resulting in a multi-objective optimization problem that is highly sensitive to the choice of loss weights and can lead to poor convergence and reduced accuracy. To address this challenge, we construct a simple transformation, exploiting the mathematical structure of trajectory optimization problems, to enforce boundary conditions exactly a-priori. This transformation can be interpreted as a reparameterization of the solution space that embeds the boundary conditions directly into the function. This converts the original constrained optimization problem into an unconstrained one over admissible trajectories. I.e. the transformation eliminates the boundary condition penalty terms and reduces the problem to a single-objective optimization. Crucially, trajectory optimization comes with a low-dimensional boundary, which allows particularly simple and stable constructions of distance functions compared to general domains in partial differential equations. Numerical experiments demonstrate that the proposed approach meaningfully improves convergence behavior and solution accuracy.

AI.brief_summary: 用神经网络把航天器位置表示为时间的函数，以无监督方式在目标中嵌入物理定律并最小化推力来优化轨迹；提出一种利用轨迹优化问题结构的变换，将边界条件先验地精确嵌入解空间，把带约束问题化为无约束单目标优化，从而去掉边界惩罚项及其权重敏感问题。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「重参数化使约束按构造满足」的训练思路可能为 latent 推理轨迹的监督提供借鉴，例如以结构化映射替代加权的起止状态惩罚项；但需核查该低维边界下的构造能否迁移到高维隐状态约束。
